newsitem.title: UK: YEAREND-Germany's DAX to consolidate gains in 97.
newsitem.headline: YEAREND-Germany's DAX to consolidate gains in 97.

text.p: German shares are likely to consolidate gains next year as corporate profits grow, with the DAX-30 index breaking above a psychological barrier of 3,000 points, a Reuters survey of the outlook for the world's top stock markets showed on Wednesday.

Forecasts for the main German index from nine equity specialists closely hugged the market's December 5 all-time high of 2,914.6, the highest forecast being 3,300 and the lowest 2,850. The mean forecast was around 3,060 points.
The market closed at 2890.95 points on Tuesday.
No contributor was able to give forecasts for 1998. Some said the outlook was too uncertain.
Following is a selection of quotes from analysts who predicted the end-1997 DAX-30 level in this survey:
GERHARD GREBE, RESEARCH DIRECTOR AT BANK JULIUS BAER

"It is a very ambitious goal, but I think the German bourse can reach the 3,200 level next year." New highs would be fuelled by a pick-up in European growth and higher German corporate profits as companies reaped the benefits of wide restructuring programmes. Grebe saw no rise in interest rates before early 1998.
"The driving forces of the stock market are still liquidity and low interest rates. The company profits of DAX firms will climb 15 percent next year.
"As the euro (single European currency) approaches, the dollar will become more and more important and...could trade between 1.50 marks and 1.62 marks."

"We expect that the DAX could fluctuate in a wide band between 2,650 and 3,100 points. In February there could be some weakness and then in May/June some strengthening, when a profit-induced rally will be triggered. Then interest rates could start to rise and the DAX will fall back down to 2,850."

"There will be a moderate but stable economic recovery next year. Maastricht is holding growth back and for the stock market we have a neutral picture." But Bewerunge saw a peak to the economic cycle in 1998 with double-digit corporate profits growth, adding that the Bundesbank "would not want to put the brakes on the economy" with higher interest rates.
